week_in_brief: The delivery moment and the decision moment are splitting apart—and AI is accelerating the gap.

items.headline: Speed Beats Breadth When Shoppers Order Online
items.whats_happening: FMI research shows delivery speed is now more damaging to conversion and loyalty than it was a year ago, while DoorDash is signing regional grocers (Brookshire, Harps, Market of Choice) to expand marketplace selection. Meanwhile, shoppers are using online for planned stock-ups (65% cite time savings) but returning to stores when they want control over product selection and to avoid delivery fees.
items.so_what: If your delivery isn't within 1-2 hours, you're losing margin to DoorDash partnerships or ceding baskets entirely. Speed is the new table stakes—breadth of selection matters less than fulfillment reliability.

items.headline: Phone-in-Store Behavior Requires Marketing That Bridges Both Worlds
items.whats_happening: Kroger research reveals 80% of omnichannel shoppers use their phones while shopping in-store for coupons, lists, and navigation. 39% discover products online then buy in-store; 34% do the reverse. Meanwhile, Google search ads are shifting away from keyword logic toward intent-based targeting that rewards creative relevance and message-match between ad copy and landing pages.
items.so_what: Your store marketing and digital campaigns are no longer separate channels—they're one blended journey. Weak landing pages or generic ad copy get punished faster now. Align in-store signage, digital coupons, and paid search messaging so shoppers experience consistency across every touch:ctage.

items.headline: SNAP Policy Changes Are Driving Brand Switching at 2x the National Rate
items.whats_happening: Ibotta analysis of SNAP purchases in five states with new federal waivers shows sugary beverage and candy purchases dropped 15-19.5—roughly 2x the national rate. More critically, 60% of SNAP shoppers say they'd trade down to private label if their preferred national brand loses SNAP eligibility. Meanwhile, retail media platforms (Amazon, Walmart, grocery apps) are capturing budget share from Google and Meta because they own transaction data and operate in closed-loop systems with logged-in users.
items.so_what: SPAP system is now a material lever for private label growth and brand switching. If you're a regional grocer, this is your moment to promote store brands to value-conscious shoppers. If you're a CPG partner, test price points and pack sizes now before larger states follow suit—and shift ad spend into retail media channels where you can measure impact directly.

items.headline: AI-Powered Martech Is Moving from Recommendations into Autonomous Execution
items.whats_happening: This week's martech releases show AI agents expanding beyond reporting into autonomous execution: adMarketplace is placing ads directly in AI search results, Braze is automating campaign orchestration across channels, and tools like Conductor are tracking brand visibility in AI-generated answers. Meanwhile, 64% of shoppers are now familiar with generative AI, and 56% have used it for food-related tasks. Agentic shopping—AI agents making purchase decisions for users—is emerging.
items.so_what: Your marketing stack is consolidating from many single-purpose tools into fewer, more agentic platforms. Before adding another tool, audit the data foundation—first-party data activation, customer identity resolution, and cross-channel attribution are the competitive advantages now. And if your brand isn't showing up in ChatGPT or Gemini responses when shoppers ask for meal ideas or shopping lists, you're invisible to the next wave of demand.

this_weeks_take: The grocery industry is splitting into two games: competing for the delivery moment (speed, convenience, AI agents) and competing for the store moment (control, discovery, phone-in-hand). Regional grocers who win will stop treating online and in-store as separate channels and start building one seamless, mobile-first journey. The shoppers are already there.
